name: Peah (Corner of Field — Detailed Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of peah: minimum amount, when and how to leave it, what divides a field for peah purposes, which crops are subject, and distribution to the poor

name: Leket (Gleanings — Detailed Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of leket: what constitutes a gleaning vs. owner's property, fallen grain from hand/sickle, ant holes, harvesting by night or blind person

name: Shikchah (Forgotten Sheaf — Detailed Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of shikchah: what qualifies as forgotten, end-of-row rules, sheaves of two seahs, trees (especially olives), standing grain saving sheaves, intentional forgetting

name: Olelot (Defective Grape Clusters)
notes: Laws of defective clusters of grapes left for the poor: definition (lacking shoulder and pendant), single grapes, entirely defective vineyard, timing of poor's access

name: Maaser Ani (Poor Tithe — Detailed Laws)
notes: Detailed laws of poor man's tithe: trustworthiness of am haaretz regarding it, minimum amounts for distribution, sharecropper's rights, who may take it

name: Divisions of a Field for Agricultural Gifts
notes: What physical features (streams, roads, paths, fallow land, different species) divide a field requiring separate peah from each section; applies to trees and vines as well

name: Hefker for the Poor (Declaring Field Ownerless)
notes: Laws regarding declaring produce ownerless for the poor: debate between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel on whether hefker for poor alone is valid hefker; effect on tithe obligations

name: Trustworthiness (Ne'emanut) Regarding Agricultural Gifts to Poor
notes: Rules on when an am haaretz is trusted to identify produce as leket, shikchah, peah, or poor tithe; distinctions based on processing stage (raw vs. cooked, whole vs. ground)

name: Minimum Amounts of Charity Distribution
notes: Minimum quantities to be given to the poor from the threshing floor: wheat, barley, spelt, dried figs, wine, oil; minimum for wandering poor (loaf, overnight needs, Shabbat meals)

name: Tamchui and Kuppah (Charity Dish and Communal Fund)
notes: Distinction between the tamchui (charity plate for daily food) and kuppah (weekly communal fund); eligibility thresholds (two meals vs. fourteen meals vs. 200 zuz); collection by two, distribution by three

name: Eligibility for Charity and Agricultural Gifts
notes: Thresholds for eligibility to take leket/shikchah/peah/maaser ani vs. communal charity; 200 zuz threshold, assets mortgaged to creditor or ketubah, exempt from selling house or tools

name: Fourth Year Vineyard — Peah and Poor Gifts
notes: Dispute between Bet Shammai and Bet Hillel on whether peret and olelot apply to fourth-year vineyard, and whether all fruit goes to the winepress

name: Sharecropper's Obligations for Agricultural Gifts
notes: Laws governing whether a sharecropper (aris) is permitted or forbidden to take leket, shikchah, peah, and maaser ani; depends on terms of sharecropping agreement

name: Hekdesh and Exemption from Agricultural Gifts
notes: Effect of dedication to Temple (hekdesh) on obligations of peah, leket, shikchah, and tithes; timing of dedication and redemption affects liability

name: Convert's Obligation for Agricultural Gifts
notes: A non-Jew who converts after harvesting his field is exempt from leket, shikchah, and peah; dispute regarding shikchah since liability arises at binding time

name: Land Requirement for Prozbul
notes: Rabbi Akiva's view that any size of land is sufficient to write a prozbul; minimum land size debate among Tannaim

name: Deathbed Gift — Retention of Land
notes: Laws of deathbed gifts: validity requires retention of any land; if no land retained, gift is invalid; assigning land to wife causes loss of ketubah

name: Manumission of Slave Through Property Gift
notes: Master who gives all his property to his slave in writing thereby frees the slave; if master retains any portion, slave is not freed; dispute about exception clause

name: Mitzvot Without a Defined Measure (Ein Lahem Shiur)
notes: Category of mitzvot for which no minimum measure is prescribed: peah, bikkurim, re'iyah, gemilut chasadim, talmud Torah; discussed in Mishnah Peah 1:1

name: Shikchah for Olive Trees
notes: Special laws of forgotten sheaf applied to olive trees: named trees exempt, trees with two seahs, trees between rows, timing after second rainfall; Rabbi Yose's opinion that no shikchah applies to olive trees
